source_meta._title: Lag spike when crossing certain chunk borders

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.14.4 using an unmodified vanilla dedicated server and a matching unmodified vanilla client. Generate a fresh default Overworld from seed -4952361208952771886. Use one test player with access to the dedicated-server console or operator permission. Do not use Paper, Spigot, Fabric, Forge, OptiFine, or other modifications for this reproduction.
preconditions: The official Minecraft Java Edition 1.14.4 client and dedicated-server software are available.
A fresh server directory is available, its EULA has been accepted, and no existing world data will be reused.
The test player can connect to the dedicated server.
The executor can use the dedicated-server console to grant the test player operator permission.
Keyboard and mouse controls are available; where controls have been rebound, use the bindings corresponding to chat, jump/fly, forward movement, debug screen, and chunk-border display.
The trigger must be performed while walking on the ground, not while flying or teleporting.

steps.action: Prepare a clean, unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.14.4 dedicated server and launch the matching unmodified 1.14.4 client. Do not install server plugins, client mods, optimization mods, or bug-fix mods.
steps.success_cue: Both client and server identify their version as Minecraft Java Edition 1.14.4, and the server contains no mods or plugins.

steps.action: Before the server generates its world for the first time, open server.properties and configure the supplied seed and the default world type. If a world was already generated under the configured level-name, stop the server and move or delete that world directory before continuing so the seed is actually applied.
steps.success_cue: server.properties contains the exact negative seed -4952361208952771886 and specifies the default world type, with no previously generated world remaining under the selected level-name.

steps.action: For this deterministic run, set the dedicated server's chunk view distance to 10 in server.properties. This fixes a concrete view-distance value because the report states that the location of the lag-producing border is relative to server view-distance.
steps.success_cue: server.properties contains view-distance=10.

steps.action: Start the dedicated server and wait for initial world generation to finish. Do not let the test player connect until the server console reports that startup is complete.
steps.success_cue: The server console displays its normal completion message containing "Done", and it accepts console input.

steps.action: In the dedicated-server console, grant operator permission to the test player's Minecraft username. Enter the command without a leading slash, replacing the placeholder with the actual username.
steps.success_cue: The server console confirms that the named player has been made a server operator.

steps.action: From the matching 1.14.4 client, connect the operator player to the dedicated server. Wait until the Overworld terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the server's Overworld, nearby terrain is visible, and movement is responsive.

steps.action: Set the client's Render Distance to 10 chunks: press Esc, select Options, select Video Settings, adjust Render Distance to 10 chunks, and return to the game.
steps.success_cue: The Video Settings screen shows Render Distance: 10 chunks, and the player has returned to gameplay.

steps.action: Put the player in Creative mode for deterministic setup. Press T to open chat, enter the exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The game confirms Creative mode, and the player has Creative abilities.

steps.action: Double-tap the Jump control, which is Space by default, to begin Creative flight. Ascend slightly if necessary and verify that releasing Space does not make the player fall.
steps.success_cue: The player is flying and can remain suspended safely while the setup commands are executed.

steps.action: Load the test location before placing its two marker blocks. Press T, enter the exact teleport command including the leading slash, press Enter, and wait until the surrounding chunks render. The elevated Y coordinate keeps the flying player clear of terrain during setup.
steps.success_cue: The player is flying above the area around X=143, Z=-371, and the surrounding terrain has finished rendering.

steps.action: Place a solid marker block at the first exact test coordinate. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter. Stone is used because the report does not specify a block type.
steps.success_cue: A stone block occupies block coordinate X=143, Y=63, Z=-371, and command feedback does not report an unloaded-position error.

steps.action: Place the adjacent solid marker block at the second exact test coordinate. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A stone block occupies block coordinate X=144, Y=63, Z=-371, directly adjacent to the first marker block across the X=144 chunk boundary.

steps.action: Load the location where the elevated block must be installed. Press T, enter the exact teleport command including the leading slash, press Enter, and wait for the destination chunks to render.
steps.success_cue: The flying player is above the area containing block coordinate X=307, Y=96, Z=-302, and the destination terrain has rendered.

steps.action: Place the single elevated block that the report identifies as creating the test condition. Press T, enter the exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter. Do not remove or replace this block before the trigger step.
steps.success_cue: A stone block occupies exact block coordinate X=307, Y=96, Z=-302, and command feedback does not report an unloaded-position error.

steps.action: Set the world's spawn point to the report's exact coordinates. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The game confirms that world spawn has been set to X=227, Y=66, Z=-376.

steps.action: Teleport to the center of the western test block. Press T, enter the exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter. Wait until all nearby terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The player's feet are at approximately X=143.5, Y=64, Z=-370.5, directly on top of the block at 143 63 -371; the player is west of the X=144 chunk boundary and movement is responsive.

steps.action: Return to grounded movement. If Creative flight is still active, double-tap the Jump control, Space by default, once to disable flight. Do not move horizontally while doing this.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on the X=143 marker block and no longer remains suspended when stepping off an edge or pressing movement controls.

steps.action: Enable the chunk-border overlay by holding F3 and pressing G. On keyboards where function keys require an Fn modifier, use the equivalent input. Keep the overlay enabled for the trigger.
steps.success_cue: Colored chunk-border lines are visible, including the vertical boundary at X=144 between the two marker blocks.

steps.action: Open the debug screen with F3 if necessary, then turn with the mouse until the player faces east, toward increasing X and the block at X=144. Do not cross the border yet.
steps.success_cue: The debug screen reports that the player is facing east, toward positive X; the player remains centered near X=143.5 on the western marker block.

steps.action: Begin the report's back-and-forth movement by walking normally east across the visible X=144 chunk boundary. Hold the Forward control, W by default, only until the player is centered on the adjacent marker block at approximately X=144.5, then release it. Do not sprint, jump, fly, or teleport during this crossing. This west-to-east crossing toward the configured spawn area is the trigger action; hand control to the observation subsystem immediately after it.
steps.success_cue: The grounded player has crossed from the block at 143 63 -371 to the block at 144 63 -371, is now in the chunk immediately east of the X=144 boundary, and the elevated block and configured world spawn remain unchanged.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just walked east across the X=144 chunk boundary from the marker block at 143 63 -371 onto the marker block at 144 63 -371. World spawn remains at 227 66 -376, the elevated block remains at 307 96 -302, the player is grounded, and the chunk-border overlay remains visible. Begin observation immediately; if the observation subsystem requires additional samples, it may direct the player to walk back and forth over the same two blocks without changing any setup state.
uncertainties: The report does not specify an exact server view-distance or client Render Distance for the supplied coordinates. This plan uses 10 chunks for both as a fixed practical configuration; the report warns that changing server type or view-distance can move the affected border.
The report does not specify the material of any of the three placed blocks. This plan uses minecraft:stone as a simple solid full block while preserving every supplied coordinate.

The report specifies a vanilla 1.14.4 server but comments contain differing results for dedicated servers, Realms, and singleplayer. This plan follows the primary description and uses a vanilla dedicated server.

The report says to walk back and forth but does not explicitly identify the first direction. This plan begins west of X=144 and crosses east toward the configured spawn point, then hands off immediately so a brief performance event can be observed; subsequent reverse and repeat crossings may be performed by the observation subsystem.
The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode and flight are used only to install the deterministic setup; flight is disabled and the trigger itself is performed as grounded normal walking.

source_meta._title: GPU usage in latest snapshot significantly higher than before, causing lag or crash for some users

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition using an unmodified vanilla client. Use snapshot 20w21a only to collect a reference interval, then reproduce in affected snapshot 20w22a on the same computer, graphics driver, display, launcher game directory, world copy, camera position, and video settings. Prefer a fixed 1920×1080 fullscreen display mode, 16-chunk render distance, VSync disabled, and an unlimited maximum frame rate, matching the detailed comparison in the report. Use an operating-system or GPU-vendor monitoring utility capable of recording GPU utilization over time. Keep the computer connected to external power, use a fixed power/performance mode, and close unrelated GPU-intensive programs.
preconditions: The launcher must be able to install and start the historical snapshots 20w21a and 20w22a.
Use 20w22a as the affected test version. Do not substitute the fix version, 1.16 Pre-release 1.
Use the same physical computer, GPU, graphics-driver installation, monitor, display resolution, power mode, and launcher JVM configuration for both version runs.
Use a clean vanilla game directory with no mods, third-party shader system, or custom resource packs enabled.
Do not install or enable any of the attached MC-186075 Shader Patch resource packs; those packs are workarounds intended to reduce the condition being reproduced.
An OS-level or GPU-vendor monitoring utility must be ready to record or graph Minecraft's GPU utilization. Configure it so data continues to be captured while Minecraft is fullscreen.
Close unrelated games, video playback, screen effects, and other GPU-intensive applications before collecting either interval.

Use only one affected-version sampling interval unless repetition is specifically requested. The report includes isolated reports of freezes, crashes, high temperatures, and system restarts, so do not repeatedly relaunch 20w22a to exaggerate the condition.
Ensure there is enough free storage to make a separate backup copy of the reference world before it is opened in 20w22a.

steps.action: Close unrelated GPU-intensive applications, connect the computer to external power if it is a laptop, and select a fixed operating-system power mode that will remain unchanged for both runs.
steps.success_cue: No unrelated GPU-intensive workload is running, and the computer's power source and power mode are fixed for the comparison.

steps.action: Set the display to a fixed 1920×1080 mode if the hardware supports it. If 1920×1080 is unavailable, select one supported resolution and record it so exactly the same resolution is used in both snapshots.
steps.success_cue: The operating system is using the recorded fixed display resolution.

steps.action: Create or select a clean launcher game directory dedicated to this test. Both snapshot installations must use this same directory so they share the same options and saves, but it must not contain mods or test-altering resource packs.
steps.success_cue: A dedicated vanilla game directory exists and can be selected by both launcher installations.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, enable snapshot or historical version visibility if required, create a baseline installation that selects exactly version 20w21a, and point it at the dedicated test directory.
steps.success_cue: The launcher shows an installation whose selected version is exactly 20w21a.

steps.action: Create a second launcher installation that selects exactly affected version 20w22a and points it at the same dedicated test directory.
steps.success_cue: The launcher shows a separate installation whose selected version is exactly 20w22a.

steps.action: Open the OS-level or GPU-vendor monitoring utility. Select the GPU used by Minecraft and enable a utilization graph or logging mode that can distinguish the baseline and affected sampling intervals.
steps.success_cue: The monitor is displaying or logging GPU utilization and will continue recording when Minecraft is fullscreen.

steps.action: Launch the 20w21a baseline installation. At the main menu, verify that the displayed version text is 20w21a before continuing.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft has reached its main menu and the menu identifies the running version as 20w21a.

steps.action: Open the resource-pack menu and ensure that only Minecraft's built-in default resources are active. Disable every custom pack, especially any attachment named MC-186075 Shader Patch.
steps.success_cue: No custom resource pack or shader patch is listed as active.

steps.action: Open Video Settings. Set Render Distance to 16 chunks, turn VSync off, and set Max Framerate to Unlimited. Leave all other graphics options at stable chosen values and record them; those values must not be changed between runs.
steps.exact_input: Options -> Video Settings; Render Distance: 16 chunks; Use VSync: OFF; Max Framerate: Unlimited
steps.success_cue: Render Distance is 16 chunks, VSync is disabled, Max Framerate is Unlimited, and the remaining video-option values have been recorded.

steps.action: Enter fullscreen mode using the Fullscreen option or the default F11 fullscreen control. Confirm that Minecraft is rendering at the fixed display resolution selected earlier.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft occupies the fullscreen display at the recorded fixed resolution.

steps.action: Return to the main menu and create a new single-player world named MC-186075-baseline. Use Creative mode and default world generation, leave the seed field blank because the report supplies no seed, and use Peaceful difficulty to prevent unrelated hostile-mob interruptions.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World; World Name: MC-186075-baseline; Game Mode: Creative; Difficulty: Peaceful; Seed: blank; World Type: Default
steps.success_cue: The new world begins loading under 20w21a with the specified test name and settings.

steps.action: After entering the world, wait without starting the measurement until surrounding terrain has rendered, newly appearing chunk boundaries have stopped filling the view, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The spawn-area terrain is visible, chunk loading has settled, and player movement responds normally.

steps.action: Choose a stationary outdoor view at or near the current spawn position. Do not build, explore, spawn entities, or add blocks. Press F3 to display the debug screen and record the player's X, Y, and Z coordinates plus the facing direction and camera angles shown there.
steps.success_cue: The F3 debug overlay is visible, and the exact player position and view direction have been recorded for matching in 20w22a.

steps.action: With the F3 overlay still visible, release all movement controls and keep the camera completely still. In the GPU monitor, place a marker or start a new baseline capture interval.
steps.exact_input: Release W, A, S, D, Space, Left Shift, and mouse movement; mark interval as 20w21a-baseline
steps.success_cue: The player is motionless in the recorded view and the GPU utility is recording a clearly identified 20w21a baseline interval.

steps.action: Leave 20w21a rendering the unchanged scene for 60 seconds. Do not move the player or camera, open menus, change focus, or modify any graphics setting during this interval.
steps.success_cue: A continuous 60-second 20w21a reference interval has been captured with the same scene and no player input.

steps.action: Press Escape, choose Save and Quit to Title, and then close Minecraft completely. Wait until the Java game process has ended before modifying the save.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title -> Quit Game
steps.success_cue: Minecraft 20w21a is closed and its Java process is no longer running.

steps.action: In the dedicated game directory's saves folder, make a complete copy of the MC-186075-baseline world folder. Preserve the original as a backup and name the copy MC-186075-20w22a. The copied world retains the player position and camera direction used for the baseline.
steps.success_cue: Two separate save folders exist: an untouched baseline backup and a copy designated for opening in 20w22a.

steps.action: Launch the affected 20w22a installation. At the main menu, verify that the displayed version text is exactly 20w22a.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft has reached its main menu and the menu identifies the running version as 20w22a.

steps.action: Before entering the world, verify that no custom resource pack is active and that Render Distance remains 16 chunks, VSync remains off, Max Framerate remains Unlimited, all other recorded video options are unchanged, and fullscreen uses the same fixed resolution as the baseline.
steps.exact_input: Options -> Resource Packs; Options -> Video Settings; F11 if fullscreen is not active
steps.success_cue: 20w22a is using default resources and exactly the same recorded display and video configuration as 20w21a.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, select the copied MC-186075-20w22a world, and choose Play Selected World. If Minecraft displays a version-upgrade or backup warning, confirm opening only the copied world; do not open or overwrite the preserved baseline backup.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> MC-186075-20w22a -> Play Selected World; confirm any warning for the copied world
steps.success_cue: The copied reference world is loading in affected snapshot 20w22a while the original baseline save remains untouched.

steps.action: Wait until the saved scene has rendered, surrounding chunks have stopped visibly filling in, and movement responds normally. Do not explore or rotate the camera while waiting.
steps.success_cue: The copied world is fully responsive and the saved scene is rendered without intentional player or camera movement.

steps.action: Press F3 to show the debug overlay. Verify that it identifies version 20w22a and compare the displayed X, Y, Z coordinates and facing values with the baseline record. If the copied save did not preserve the view exactly, use minimal movement and mouse input to restore the recorded position and facing, then release all controls.
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay identifies 20w22a, and the player is stationary at the baseline coordinates with the baseline camera direction restored.

steps.action: In the GPU monitoring utility, place a new marker or begin a fresh interval labeled 20w22a-affected. Immediately return focus to Minecraft if necessary, leave the F3 overlay visible, and keep the player and camera completely still.
steps.exact_input: Mark interval as 20w22a-affected; release W, A, S, D, Space, Left Shift, and mouse movement
steps.success_cue: The monitor is capturing a clearly identified affected-version interval while 20w22a continuously renders the same stationary scene and settings used for the baseline.

stor.handoff_condition: The GPU monitor has just begun the marked 20w22a-affected interval. Minecraft 20w22a is fullscreen and focused, default resources are active, the copied baseline world and surrounding chunks are fully loaded, the F3 overlay is visible, and the player is stationary at the recorded baseline coordinates and camera direction. Begin observing GPU utilization, frame rate, responsiveness, and process stability without changing the scene or settings.
uncertainties: The report contains no formal Steps to Reproduce section, deterministic seed, coordinates, world download, exact scene, or required game mode. The clean Creative-mode world and stationary spawn-area scene are practical choices for obtaining a repeatable comparison.
20w21a is used only as the comparison baseline because many report comments directly compare it with 20w22a. It is not added to affected_versions because the report lists only 20w22a as affected.

The 1920×1080 fullscreen resolution, 16-chunk render distance, and uncapped frame rate are taken from a detailed comparison in the report and are not stated as universal requirements. If the machine cannot use 1920×1080, one fixed supported resolution must be used unchanged for both runs.
The 60-second reference interval is not specified by the report; it is a practical measurement duration selected to obtain a stable baseline.
The exact GPU-monitoring interface is operating-system and hardware-vendor dependent. The report demonstrates GPU utilization measurements but does not prescribe a particular monitoring program.

The issue was reported across many different GPUs and operating systems, with substantially different magnitudes. Reproduction strength therefore depends on the available GPU, driver, display resolution, and whether the system is CPU- or GPU-limited.

Opening a copied 20w21a world in 20w22a is a practical method for preserving the same scene. The report also states that the condition occurred in both existing saves and newly generated worlds, so world conversion is not asserted to be a bug requirement.
Some comments report freezes, crashes, high temperatures, or system restarts, but these outcomes were intermittent and are not made reproduction requirements.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.16.5 in a fresh client session; authenticated account with working internet connectivity; unmodified singleplayer world running on the integrated server and not opened to LAN. Use the first player-authored chat message of the session for the trigger attempt.
preconditions: Use Minecraft Java Edition, not Bedrock Edition.
Configure the launcher to start the exact affected release 1.16.5.
Remain signed in to an authenticated Minecraft account and keep internet connectivity available. A report comment states that the issue did not reproduce in offline mode.
Completely restart the Minecraft client before the attempt. Supplied comments indicate that later messages may not trigger the event again until the client is restarted.

Do not submit any chat messages or commands before the designated trigger step. Command feedback and some other generated messages were also reported as related triggers and could invalidate the first-message condition.
Use a singleplayer world loaded through the Singleplayer menu. Do not select the Open to LAN option during the session.
If performance recording or frame-time monitoring will be used by the observation subsystem, start it before submitting the message because the trigger is a short, immediate event.

steps.action: If Minecraft is already running, use the title-screen Quit Game button or close the game window, then wait until the Minecraft client has completely exited before continuing.
steps.success_cue: No Minecraft game window remains open and the previous client session has ended.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher while signed in and connected to the internet. Create or select an installation whose version is the exact Java Edition release listed below; do not select the fixed snapshot 21w39a or a newer release.
steps.success_cue: The selected launcher installation identifies its game version as 1.16.5.

steps.action: Launch the selected 1.16.5 installation and wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition main menu is responsive and displays version 1.16.5.

steps.action: From the main menu, click Singleplayer.
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is open.

steps.action: Select an available singleplayer world and click Play Selected. If no world exists, click Create New World, leave the world-generation and game-mode settings at their defaults, optionally name it "MC-218167 Test", and click Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The game begins loading a singleplayer world.

steps.action: Wait until the player has entered the world, nearby terrain has rendered, and normal movement and camera input respond without chunk-loading pauses.
steps.success_cue: The world is fully visible, the player can move normally, and no loading screen is present.

steps.action: Keep the world as a private singleplayer session. Do not use Esc -> Open to LAN, and do not join or start a multiplayer server.
steps.success_cue: The current world was entered from the Singleplayer menu and no Open to LAN action has been performed during this session.

steps.action: Confirm that no player-authored chat message or command has been submitted since the client was launched. If any message or command was already submitted, abort this attempt, completely exit Minecraft, and restart from step 1.
steps.success_cue: This is still a fresh client session with no previously submitted chat messages or commands.

steps.action: Open the chat input using the Open Chat control, which is T by default. Wait until the chat overlay and its input field are visible and responsive before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The chat overlay is open with an empty text-entry field at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Type the sample non-command message below into the chat field. Do not include a leading slash, and do not press Enter yet.
steps.success_cue: The complete text "MC-218167 test message" is visible in the chat input field and has not yet been submitted.

steps.action: Press Enter once to submit the message. Do not send a second message during this attempt, and immediately hand control to the performance observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The first player-authored chat message of the fresh client session has been submitted and no second message has been entered.

stor.handoff_condition: The first non-command chat message of the fresh Minecraft 1.16.5 client session has just been submitted by pressing Enter while the player remains in a singleplayer world that has not been opened to LAN. Begin observing client responsiveness immediately and do not submit another message during this attempt.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a required world seed, coordinates, dimension, game mode, difficulty, graphics setting, or world-generation setting; default settings are used only as a practical execution choice.
The issue is explicitly described as intermittent, so one correctly prepared attempt may not reproduce it.

The report states that the issue generally does not occur twice in a row. Supplied comments further describe it as affecting the first message and not recurring until the client is restarted; the fresh-client and first-message conditions are therefore used to improve reproducibility.

A supplied comment reports that the issue no longer occurred in offline mode, so authenticated online operation with internet connectivity is included even though it is not present in the formal two-step reproduction section.
Comments disagree about whether graphics hardware affects reproducibility; no GPU vendor or model is imposed as a requirement.
The exact chat text is not specified. "MC-218167 test message" is a harmless practical substitute for the report's instruction to type something.

Although later comments mention multiplayer and later versions such as 1.18.1, the formal report specifically requests a singleplayer world not opened to LAN, and only the versions in the report's Affects versions field are included here.

source_meta._title: GUI / Item rendering can heavily impact frame rate performance

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.17.1 in an unmodified single-player client; a Superflat world using the "The Void" preset; Creative mode as a practical setup choice; one completely empty double chest and one double chest with all 54 storage slots occupied; the Alt+F3 frame-time graph enabled during the comparison.
preconditions: Install and launch Minecraft Java Edition 1.17.1, the first version listed as affected in the report. Do not use fix version 25w16a for the reproduction.
Use the vanilla client without rendering or performance mods so that a third-party renderer does not alter the GUI-rendering workload.
Use Creative mode to make chest placement and deterministic filling possible without crafting or gathering resources. Creative mode is not specified by the report and is only an execution choice.
Keep the same game window size, GUI scale, resource packs, video settings, frame-rate limit, VSync state, and camera conditions for the empty- and full-chest trials.
Ensure the keyboard can send F3-key combinations. On keyboards where F3 is assigned a hardware function, the Fn key may also be necessary.
The report does not identify a particular item. This plan uses full stacks of Diamonds as a consistent, stackable, non-block item available in 1.17.1.
Keep the mouse pointer over the same non-slot portion of the chest GUI during both trials so that item tooltips are not introduced into only one measurement.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation for Java Edition 1.17.1, start the game, and wait for the main title screen to become responsive.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left corner of the title screen identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.17.1, and the menu buttons respond normally.

steps.action: Open the single-player world creation screen by selecting "Singleplayer" and then "Create New World".
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Set the new world's game mode to Creative. Leave cheats enabled if the world-creation screen enables them automatically for Creative mode; no commands are required by this plan.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays "Game Mode: Creative".

steps.action: Configure the world as a void world: select "More World Options...", cycle "World Type" until it reads "Superflat", select "Customize", select "Presets", choose "The Void", select "Use Preset", and return with "Done". The Void preset and its spawn platform are available in the selected Java Edition version. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_15w37a?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: More World Options... -> World Type: Superflat -> Customize -> Presets -> The Void -> Use Preset -> Done
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows the Superflat world type configured with the "The Void" preset.

steps.action: Select "Create New World". After the world opens, do not begin chest setup until the spawn platform and surrounding void have rendered and movement, inventory input, and camera movement respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing or flying above a small solid spawn platform surrounded by empty void, and game input is responsive.

steps.action: Obtain chests from the Creative inventory. Press E, open the "Search Items" tab if it is not already selected, click the search field, enter "chest", and place a stack of the ordinary Chest item into a hotbar slot. Press E again to close the inventory. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the gameplay screen.
steps.exact_input: E; search text: chest; item: Chest
steps.success_cue: A Chest stack is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots and normal gameplay view is restored.

steps.action: Create the double chest that will be filled. Select the Chest hotbar slot, aim at the top of the spawn platform, and right-click once to place a chest. Aim at the top of the immediately adjacent platform block and right-click again while facing the same direction so the two chests join. Keep open platform space around the pair.
steps.exact_input: Select Chest; right-click twice on two horizontally adjacent platform blocks
steps.success_cue: Two adjacent chest blocks have joined into one double-width chest.

steps.action: Create the empty control double chest. Leave at least one non-chest block between it and the first double chest, then place two adjacent chests in the same manner. Do not put any item into this second double chest.
steps.exact_input: Right-click twice on another pair of horizontally adjacent platform blocks, with at least one block separating the two chest pairs
steps.success_cue: There are two separate double chests on the platform; neither pair has joined to the other pair.

steps.action: Designate the first double chest as the full test chest and the second as the empty control chest. Open the Creative inventory with E, remove the remaining Chest stack from the hotbar using the Creative inventory's destroy-item slot, select "Search Items", enter "diamond", and locate the Diamond item.
steps.exact_input: E; search text: diamond; item: Diamond
steps.success_cue: The Diamond item is visible in the Creative item catalog, and no Chest stack remains in the hotbar.

steps.action: Prepare the first batch of item stacks. For each of the nine hotbar slots, take a full Diamond stack from the Creative item catalog and place it into that hotbar slot. Close the inventory with E when all nine hotbar slots contain 64 Diamonds.
steps.success_cue: All nine hotbar slots contain full stacks of 64 Diamonds.

steps.action: Transfer the first batch into the full test chest. Aim at that double chest and right-click to open it. Hold Shift and left-click each of the nine Diamond stacks in the hotbar so each stack moves into the chest. Do not transfer anything into the empty control chest.
steps.exact_input: Right-click full test chest; Shift+left-click each of 9 Diamond stacks
steps.success_cue: Nine of the double chest's 54 storage slots contain Diamond stacks, and the player's hotbar is empty.

steps.action: Press Esc to close the chest. Repeat the following batch cycle five more times: press E, search for Diamond if necessary, load all nine hotbar slots with full Diamond stacks, close the inventory, right-click the designated full test chest, and Shift+left-click all nine stacks into it. After the fifth additional batch, keep the chest GUI open and inspect only the slot occupancy.
steps.exact_input: Repeat 5 times: E -> Diamond ×64 in all 9 hotbar slots -> E -> right-click full test chest -> Shift+left-click all 9 stacks
steps.success_cue: The full test chest GUI shows six rows of nine storage slots, and every one of its 54 slots contains a Diamond stack. The player inventory and hotbar contain no remaining Diamond stacks.

steps.action: Close the full test chest with Esc. Confirm that the other double chest has never been used for storage. If its state is uncertain, briefly open it, verify that all 54 slots are empty, and close it before enabling performance graphs.
steps.success_cue: Both chest GUIs are closed; one double chest is known to contain 54 Diamond stacks and the control double chest is known to contain no items.

steps.action: Prepare consistent comparison conditions. Stand directly in front of the empty control chest at normal interaction distance. Allow all visible terrain to finish rendering, stop moving, and avoid changing the window, video settings, GUI scale, or resource packs for the remainder of the test.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary, the empty control chest is within right-click range, surrounding rendering is stable, and game input is responsive.

steps.action: Enable the 1.17.1 frame-time graph by holding Alt and pressing F3 once. On a keyboard that reserves F3 for a hardware function, use Fn+Alt+F3. In this version, Alt+F3 opens the debug screen with the frame-time graph; the shortcut changed in later versions. ([ja.minecraft.wiki](https://ja.minecraft.wiki/w/%E3%83%87%E3%83%90%E3%83%83%E3%82%B0%E7%94%BB%E9%9D%A2?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Alt+F3 (or Fn+Alt+F3 when required by the keyboard)
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay is visible and a scrolling frame-time graph is displayed at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Place the mouse pointer over a neutral part of the screen where it will not cover a chest storage slot after the GUI opens, such as the future chest-title or GUI-background area. Keep the pointer at that corresponding location during both chest trials.
steps.success_cue: The pointer is positioned away from the 54 chest slots and will not produce an item tooltip.

steps.action: Aim at the empty control double chest and right-click it once to open its container GUI. Do not move items or change any settings.
steps.success_cue: A "Large Chest" GUI with six rows of nine empty chest slots is open, and the debug/frame-time display remains visible.

steps.action: Keep the empty chest GUI open and remain idle until the scrolling graph has accumulated a stable control sample, preferably until bars created before opening the chest have scrolled out of the graph. Retain the displayed FPS or frame-time level as the empty-chest baseline. Do not hover over slots.
steps.success_cue: A stable empty-chest baseline reading has been retained while the empty Large Chest GUI remains open.

steps.action: Press Esc to close the empty control chest. Wait until the gameplay view has returned, the chest lid has closed, and movement and camera input respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The empty chest GUI is closed, normal gameplay view is visible, and the Alt+F3 debug/frame-time display remains enabled.

steps.action: Move to the full test double chest and stop at approximately the same interaction distance and viewing angle used for the empty chest. Keep the same window, graphics settings, and pointer placement. Wait until movement has stopped and rendering is stable.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary with the full test chest within right-click range, and the debug/frame-time graph is still visible.

steps.action: Aim at the full test double chest and right-click it exactly once to open the container. Do not move the mouse onto an item slot, transfer items, close the GUI, or repeatedly reopen the chest.
steps.exact_input: Right-click full test double chest once
steps.success_cue: The "Large Chest" GUI is open with all 54 chest slots displaying Diamond stacks, while the debug/frame-time graph remains enabled.

stor.handoff_condition: The full 54-slot Diamond-filled double chest has just been opened once under the same client and rendering conditions used for the empty-chest baseline, with the Alt+F3 frame-time graph still enabled and no item tooltip displayed. Begin observing and comparing frame-rate or frame-time performance without closing or modifying the GUI.
uncertainties: The report requires a double chest "full of items" but does not specify item identity, stack size, or whether all 54 slots must contain distinct items. This plan uses Diamond ×64 in every slot as a deterministic practical interpretation.
The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is selected only to eliminate crafting and resource-gathering variability.
The report does not prescribe whether the empty or full chest should be opened first. This plan opens the empty chest first to establish a control baseline immediately before the full-chest trigger.

The report does not specify a sampling duration or an FPS-recording method. The plan uses the observable condition that the scrolling graph has replaced its pre-opening history rather than imposing a hardware-dependent number of seconds.

This execution plan is tailored to recommended version 1.17.1. Alt+F3 is the correct graph shortcut there, but the shortcut was changed to F3+2 beginning in the 1.20.2 development cycle; an executor intentionally testing later affected versions may need that later shortcut. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/rest.php/v1/page/Debug_screen/html?utm_source=openai))
